title: Formulae Handbook: motor selection and drive calculations
creator: Jan Braun / maxon academy
prerequisites: SI units, moments, angular velocity, basic algebra
access: Publicly readable manufacturer-hosted PDF; copyrighted, not an open license.
why: A compact source for checking the distinction between peak operating points and an effective thermal load.
first_task: Open section 6.5 and identify the separate RMS-torque, maximum-torque, and speed checks. Compare their meanings with the guide's ideal cycle.
limitations: Reference formulas do not qualify a chosen motor, cooling arrangement, or printed mechanism. This is a 2012 handbook, not a current product catalog.
evidence_note: Opened the 60-page official PDF; located motor selection at page index 41 and requested its rendered page. The section distinguishes RMS and maximum torque.

title: Motor Sizing Calculations
creator: Oriental Motor
prerequisites: Mass, distance, time, and unit conversion
why: Shows why motor selection requires a motion specification and more than a single torque number.
first_task: Read the selection procedure and list the inputs still missing from your own layout before using any product-selection tool.
limitations: Some explanatory wording is oversimplified: inertia does not become zero at rest; acceleration torque does. Keep the guide's SI derivation and examine unit conventions carefully.
evidence_note: Opened from the official sizing tools page. The selection procedure names inertia, torque, speed, operating environment, and final motor/gearhead checks.

title: Controller: nested loops, trajectories, and reference frames
creator: ODrive Robotics
prerequisites: Position error, torque, and feedback basics
why: A concrete implementation makes the otherwise abstract three-loop diagram inspectable.
first_task: Trace which loops remain active in position, velocity, and torque modes; identify where the guide's paper exercise deliberately simplifies the implementation.
limitations: The API and tuning details are specific to the documented drive and firmware. Reading the page is not hardware commissioning.
evidence_note: Opened the official page and read the structure, control modes, trajectory, and reference-frame sections.

title: Optical encoder FAQ: accuracy, resolution, and repeatability
creator: Renishaw
why: Prevents encoder bit depth from being mistaken for demonstrated mechanism accuracy.
first_task: Read the accuracy/resolution/repeatability question, then classify quantization, a stable zero offset, and return-position scatter separately.
limitations: The examples and product details concern Renishaw optical encoders; they are not specifications for a hobby magnetic encoder.
evidence_note: Opened the official FAQ and located the definitions plus the explanation of jitter and subdivision error.

title: Hardware Configuration: feedback, power, and thermal limits
creator: ODrive Robotics
why: Connects sensor placement to stability and temperature protection to loss of available torque.
first_task: Read Dual-Encoder and Temperature Regulation; mark which sensor closes which loop and what happens when current is thermally reduced.
limitations: Features differ among ODrive hardware models. Use the selected product's instructions; do not transpose settings to another driver.
evidence_note: Opened the page. Dual-Encoder explicitly discusses compliance/backlash and load-velocity instability; temperature sections describe current reduction and overtemperature faults.

title: API reference: torque constant and q-axis current
creator: ODrive Robotics
prerequisites: Torque/current relationship and basic field-oriented-control vocabulary
access: Public generated API documentation; observed version 0.6.12.
why: Provides an actual drive's definition of the current used to estimate motor torque.
first_task: Find Iq_measured and torque_constant. Record their units and note the documented telemetry filtering before planning measurements.
limitations: A current-based torque estimate is not an independent output-force sensor; transmission losses and mechanical compliance remain outside that estimate.
evidence_note: Opened the official API page and located Iq_measured, which is defined as torque-generating q-axis current, and torque_constant in N m/A.

title: Regen Clamp Datasheet
creator: ODrive Robotics
prerequisites: Electrical power, capacitor energy, and datasheet conditions
why: A real energy-handling device exposes the voltage, current, resistor, and thermal questions hidden by 'the motor stops.'
first_task: Identify the path of regenerated energy and the distinction between peak and continuous electrical specifications.
limitations: An example for evaluating requirements, not a recommendation that this particular product fits every small actuator.
evidence_note: Opened the official datasheet; it describes excess energy diversion to an external resistor and lists electrical, thermal, and resistor-selection sections.

title: Motor Calibration Parameters
creator: ODrive Robotics
prerequisites: Selected motor ratings and drive setup documentation
why: Shows that calibration is an energized physical procedure with its own parameter requirements.
first_task: Distinguish resistance calibration, inductance calibration, and lock-in motion before writing your own commissioning plan.
limitations: The page contains product-specific starting guidance, not universal settings. The guide intentionally supplies no executable hardware-control commands.
evidence_note: Opened the official page; it identifies required calibration current/voltage parameters and describes resistance, inductance, and lock-in behavior.
